Did you know Colette from Ratatouille turned a fancy Miami dinner into total chaos?

She had just started working at Carbone Miami, the kind of bougie restaurant where every plate is perfect and every critic can make or break the place. The night was going smoothly until a food critic walked in who once gave the rat’s cooking a brutal review. From the kitchen shelf, the rat started tugging her hair like old times, signaling exactly what he wanted her to do. Colette tried to ignore it, focusing on her station, but the pulling got more insistent and the rat clearly had revenge in mind. Before she could fully stop it, she found herself walking a pot of soup out to the dining room, heart racing. In a split second the moment happened—the soup went exactly where it should not have, the table erupted, and the entire restaurant froze in shock.

Within minutes the dining room was chaos, the manager was furious, and Colette realized the rat had just turned a classy night into a legendary mess.

#colette #ratatouille #carbone #miami #fyp

Why You Aren’t Seeing the Results You Want From Your Skincare…

To find out, listen to the audio series 'The Alpha's Bride' (FREE for a limited period of time) Click on the link below to download the PocketFM app, now!
My first touch froze my mother to gold.
I was born with golden eyes.
When she held me for the first time, 
her skin hardened beneath my fingers.
At five, I grabbed a pack boy during a game
He froze mid-laugh.
At eight, I touched a beggar’s last bread.
It became pure gold in my hands.
The pack called me cursed
But my father called me opportunity.
He bartered me 
for ten million dollars.
That was the beginning of my doom. 
Alpha Edward didn’t see a child. He saw a mine. "
He burned my palms with hot iron rods,
trying to force gold from my skin.
Something white sparks before he could break me.
And the Moon Goddess descended,
“I am taking the child’s blessing, when she turns eighteen, she will take everything from you.”
A golden light tore from my hands 
and vanished into the sky.
My power disappeared. But my suffering didn’t.
Alpha Edward grew afraid.
So he handed me to his daughter.
“Make her your slave. Suppress her before she outshines you.”
Marcy obeyed. She didn’t kill me. She ended me slowly.
Years of hunger.
Bruises.
Chains.
Servitude. "
Today, I cook for two hundred wolves without sleep everyday.
I am 18 now but nothing changed."I want to give up", I whispered to the moon goddess in pain.
I was answered. And everything was about to change in a blink.
Merge-
There were whispers through the pack. Electric, hushed, breathless. A visitor was coming.
Alpha Damon.

Leader of the Dark Howlers, fiercest pack in the realm. He was the most powerful Alpha in all of North America. Women threw themselves at him. Rulers feared him. He could seduce a she-wolf with a glance, or tear out a man’s throat just as easily.
Damon was untouchable. 
He scorned the idea of love. Rejected every political match. Not a single potential bride, despite the many presented, could win his affection. None were worthy of being his Luna, the proud she-wolf to rule by his side.
Love was a distraction, an attempt to tame him. And Damon would never be tamed. 
Still, there were those who tried. 

Alpha Edward, leader of the Red Moon pack, was desperate to secure his political power. He invited Damon to meet his daughter, Princess Marcy, beautiful, cunning, cruel. She intended to make him hers.
Talia feared their union. Would Marcy succeed where so many others had failed? Would Marcy’s cruelty only intensify as Luna to such a powerful Alpha? 

The moment Alpha Damon stepped onto Red Moon Pack grounds with his mated Betas, Caden and Maya, something felt off. His wolf stirred uneasily beneath the surface. Damon didn’t need confirmation, he already knew: no one in the Red Moon Pack could be trusted.

They all sat down in the dining hall, its gaudy opulence a reflection of Red Moon’s inflated ego.

Marcy arrived fashionably late, every detail of her appearance sharpened like a blade. Shimmering blond hair, a sculpted figure. She was the type of girl who got what she wanted.
Her friend, Nora, wasn’t as restrained. She eyed Damon with hunger, her gaze sliding over him like a caress. The rumors had reached her ears: about his appetite, his stamina, his size. She didn’t care that Marcy was supposed to win the Alpha’s hand. Nora wanted a taste for herself.
Marcy’s mother, Luna Layla, noticed the heat in Nora’s stare… and the flicker of fury in her daughter’s eyes.
“Marcy,” Layla said, too sweetly, “Why don’t you show Alpha Damon to his room so you two can… talk?”

While the Red Moon Pack celebrated Damon’s arrival, elsewhere in the kitchens, Talia worked until the sweat stung her eyes. All she could dream of was the scraps she might scavenge when the feast was over.
The other Omegas had different plans for her.
Anna, their cruel ringleader, stepped into Talia’s path, towering over her, “Listen up, slave.” The other Omegas giggled behind her like hyenas. 
Anna’s lips twisted into a cruel smirk. “You’re going to deliver towels to Alpha Damon’s room.”
Talia froze. “Right now? But... what if he’s inside?”
Anna raised her hand, ready to strike. “Are you questioning me?”
Talia flinched, her heart pounding. Without her wolf, she was defenseless against the bullies. 
Without another word, she took the towels and hurried off, every step dragging her closer to the Alpha’s quarters and whatever fate awaited her behind that door.

When Talia entered the room, she froze. Damon was in his room. But he wasn’t alone. 
There was Marcy. On her knees. Between Damon’s legs. 
Marcy whipped around, her eyes blazing with fury as they locked onto Talia’s. The insolence! 
A jolt of fear shot up Talia’s spine. Retribution would be certain.
Damon’s eyes snapped to Talia.
“Stop!” he barked.
But Talia was gone, bolting from the room, too terrified to look back.
What Talia didn’t know, what she couldn’t have known, is that in that moment, Damon’s world had shifted.
Her scent. It hit his veins like a spark of kindling, igniting something primal within him.
Could it be? His inner wolf howled the truth within him, again and again. She, a lowly omega, a serving girl without a friend, was his fated mate?

Ignoring the mocking laughter of Anna and the others, Talia ran until she reached the attic, shoving the cabinet against the door before collapsing in the corner, struggling to quiet her frantic breathing.
'Is this it? Is this the day I die?'

Back in Damon’s room, Marcy landed clumsily on her backside as Damon shoved her away, his expression thunderous and unreadable.
"Who was that girl?" he demanded, hastily buttoning his pants.
Marcy knew exactly who she was. Talia. That wolf-less bitch. How dare she step into an Alpha’s chambers uninvited? And worse, if word got out that Marcy had been pleasuring Damon before he’d even proposed... she’d be humiliated. A laughingstock. Her reputation would be in shreds.
Marcy’s jaw clenched with fury. She should’ve done more than just beat the girl this morning.
But Damon didn’t notice Marcy’s simmering rage. He was too distracted, his mind replaying the moment when she walked in. How that intoxicating scent, freesia and citrus, had struck him. How his wolf had howled, wild and urgent. All he could think about was pulling her into his arms.
'Mate.' His wolf howled.  In confirmation, I couldnt my wolf had been silenced years ago. 

My name is Talia, but no one calls me Talia except for teachers on the first day of schooling. I'm more popular as the wolfless freak. I'm a werewolf in the red moon pack. Since I'm an orphan, I'm not completely sure how old I am, but I'm pretty sure I'm 16. Also, I'm an omega, which means I'm a servant. My job is to make the meals for the werewolves who live in the pack house. Between making breakfast and dinner for over 100 wolves, cleaning up after them, and restocking the pantries of the ranked members' apartments on the 3rd and 4th floors, I do normal teenager stuff, except I don't have a lot of spare time to do so. Homework is the extent of living my teen life. Right now it's 11:30 at night. I'm putting the finishing touches on my English essay when I hear the door of the dungeon slam open. Great. Now what did I do? It doesn't take much. 
Alpha Edward is an alcoholic. It's really difficult for werewolves to get drunk, which means you have to drink heavily to feel the effects. This means he probably had a fight with Luna Layla about his drinking. Which means she locked him out of their room. Which means he has come down to take out his anger on me. Just an average Tuesday in the packhouse. I know the drill. I'm already on my feet waiting for him. I'm thinking in my mind. “Alpha Edward, what can I do for you?" I ask with my eyes looking at the floor. I keep my hands clasped in front of me, trying to look as small as possible. Without a word, a whiskey bottle whizzes past my ear and smashes against the wall above my cot. I flinch and can't help but start to tremble and hug myself. As I grab him, his eyes widen in fear and he starts howling in pain. A sizzling sound comes from where my hands connect with his skin. He quickly releases my neck and we both fall to the ground. "How are you doing this? What are you, Talia?" I stand up feeling much taller than my five-foot-tall frame. Sylvie’s voice booms from me, "I'm a warrior child of the Moon Goddess. If you tell anyone what has happened here today, I WILL MAKE YOU SUFFER," Sylvie threatens. George scoots back on his backside away from me, wide-eyed, then clambers up and runs away as fast as he can. Suddenly, I come back into my normal state of mind and I fall back to the ground, exhausted. My hands are no longer glowing but they feel like they are on and full of static electricity. " Sylvie! What was that?" I scold her, but mostly because it scared me. "I couldn't help it. He was threatening you." "Okay, but what was with the glowy purple, burnt hands thing?! That's not normal!" "Talia, we've been through this. You are a child of the Moon Goddess. You are special. There is more too. You will see after we shift for the first time. Until then, I'm not strong enough to show you. Besides, it isn't like I hurt him badly; his wolf will heal him before he is back in his office." "I-I don-, wait, you mean the Moon Goddess is my actual mom? Like she gave birth to me, specifically? Not just, like, mother of all werewolves because she created us a gazillion years ago?" "That's what I've been saying since I came. It's not my fault you didn't believe me." I picked up a towel to wipe the stain from my nose. Sylvie  is already healing me from the break. But my face is going to be bruised for a couple of days. I pull my hat down low so no one can see the bruises then pick up the first two platters and rush out to the dining room. "Okay, well if you're able to do that to George, how come you can't do it to Alpha Edward or Marcy?" "Well, I think it happened one time before, but I wasn't fully in control then. I can't do it now because he's your Alpha, Talia. I can't go against what he says. I can't attack your Alpha or his daughter." "Fine," I concede. I don't want to argue with her. I'm just trying to figure out the rules. I'm in uncharted territory here. I mean, it's cool territory but I don't know what our limits are. Once all the platters are out, I make the list of extra supplies I need and put it in the box hanging outside George's office. That way, I don't have to face him again. I clean up the dining room from lunch and still have about forty-five minutes until I need to start dinner. I decided to go to the stockroom and put supplies on the pantry cart for later. As I'm working, I hear someone clear their throat behind me. I look up to find Marcy standing uncomfortably close to me. "Can I help you with something, Marcy?" I try to swallow the panic that instantly builds in my throat. "Talia, I just wanted to say, when I'm in control of the pack, you won't be treated the way you are now," she takes a step closer, forcing me to back up against the cart. "Marcy, please stop," I put my hands up and push lightly against her to get her to move, but she's stronger than me and doesn't budge. I look up at her to see an evil grin distorting his face. "I see the way my dad treats you, Talia. You never complain. You just take it," she moves closer, breathing deeply until she's fully pressing himself against me, "I think you like when he does it. Don't you?" he whispers in my ear. What?! There is no way I heard her right. Did I? "Marcy, I do not enjoy what your father did to me," I say in disbelief, "and you're no better, standing there watching him instead of stopping him.” I can feel tears stinging the corners of my eyes as she slips an arm around my waist. I cannot believe this is happening right now. "Don't lie to me, Talia. I do like men, but I can’t deny your scent does something to me no man ever can. The way you beg before my father turns me on. It makes me crazy to think about what I'll do to you if I find you alone. I can't wait to get my hands on you. I want to hear you moan with pleasure when I am with you. I want you on your knees so I can whip you instead of him. I want you to be my toy, Talia, not his. You'd like that, wouldn't you? Bowing down to me with that pretty hairs in the air? We'll turn the dungeon into a playroom just for us, instead of just your bedroom," She's nuzzling against my neck right below my ear making me cringe, but I don't have anywhere to be able to move to get away from him. I can feel her fingers pressing against me, trying to make their way between my legs. "Are you insane?" I yell. I push hard against her but she's too strong. She doesn't budge, "Get off of me, you sicko!" This whole time, she's been turned on by watching her dad torture me? What is wrong with this family? The look on her face contorts from happy evil to disgusted. Without warning, she takes a step back. She elbows me in the back, dropping me onto the table. Then she bends over behind me, and whispers in my ears, "I know you want me, Talia. Don't worry, you'll be mine as soon as I convince my father to let me have you. I want to make him proud when I make you squeal in pain but I don't think I can wait," Her voice is rough and ragged with excitement and her hands are all over me and groping me. All I can do is sob. I'm afraid to fight back or to even say anything. Sylvie  can't help me because she's the Alpha’s daughter. 'Moon Goddess, if you're my mother, please help me! Please save me from this!' I cry in my mind as Marcy bites my ears, gropes me and her hand runs all over me under my clothes. She pulls my leggings and underwear down, tearing them both in half with her wolf claws extended. I feel her pressing her fingers against my entrance. I know what was about to happen and I can't take it anymore. I turn my mind off. Just like her father beat me within an inch of my life. My mind cannot be present for what is happening to me. She finally gets off me and I fall to the floor. She tears the back of my shirt open and strikes with her claws on my back as if to mark me as her property. I lay on the floor of the supply room crying. "Get up, Talia, " Sylvie  commands in my mind. “I said get up," she repeats. Her voice is stern but caring, "You're better than this. You will survive this." "I want to leave the world,  Sylvie . I can't do this anymore. I can't." "You can and you will. You will find your mate soon enough and things will change. I promise." "How can you be so sure?" "You will see. Glowy, burning hands are not your only gift." I get up, find an old cardigan in the back of the stockroom, and put it on. I go back to my room to find new clothes before making dinner. The next four days go without incident. Unless you consider I have gone to the roof several times contemplating my existence. Each time, I stand with my toes at the edge and stare down from the four-story building. I can't bring myself to do anything except cry and go back to my room. I can't do it to  Sylvie . I can't take her life because I want to take mine. Sunday after dinner service, I see Marcy in the hallway while I'm refilling pantries. She quickly approaches me and grabs me by the arm. She extends her claws into my bicep, drawing blood. "Talia, if you tell anyone and I mean anyone what you saw in George's office, I will make you suffer again," she says in a low threatening tone. Not again! I'm fed up. Does she want to bully me? Okay, fine. I lift my hat and let my violet eyes look directly at her. She gasps at the unusual sight. "Marcy, it would be a relief and I would welcome it. You don't care how I'm treated by this pack. Including you, your father, your mother, and your lover, too," Tears choke up in my throat. I cannot take any more punishment or threats from anyone else. I'm at my wit's end. If she takes my life right here in this hallway, it would be a relief. "I'm sorry,  Sylvie. I just can't do it anymore," I say to my angel as I'm staring down Marcy. She doesn't respond, she shuts our mind link and crawls into the corner of my mind. Marcy pushes me away, "Insolent bastard! You should be grateful for your life! The Alpha will hear about this." "I'm not grateful for this life, Marcy. And if you think I should be, you are part of the problem. If you want to tell the Alpha about this incident, I'm more than happy to tell him what instigated it." She stares at me with pure anger and hatred before walking away without a word. I guess fate has other plans for me. I stand in the hall for a few minutes to see if she is coming back, but she doesn't. I'm certain she is going to sabotage me. Maybe she's going to smother me in my sleep or just stab me straight in the back. Either way, I was serious when I told her I welcome her. I finish pantry duty making sure everything is set in the guest rooms. I had George order bouquets for each of the suites as an extra touch. In the guest Alpha's suite, I also added a bottle of champagne. If this is the last thing I ever get to do, I want it to be something that makes someone else happy. It is almost one-thirty in the morning before I plop into my bed totally exhausted. It has been a day. If Marcy has anything to do with it, it will probably be my last. Sylvie  is exhausted too. She stops sulking long enough to tell me she needs me to shift, but I can't. I have no time or energy. I keep promising her I will, but I feel like I've broken that promise. I float off to the sounds of her whimpering in my head while I cry into the pillow. To my surprise, my alarm wakes me in the morning. Sylvie  makes me promise to hang on for one more day. We go through the motions of the life I hate. While I'm getting ready, I look in the mirror to find my hair is completely silvery now. I tuck it into a bun to try to avoid people noticing it. The delegation from Dark Howlers arrives in the early afternoon. They are all tall and intimidating with tattoos and big muscles. Some of them have visible scars on their arms and faces. They're wearing matching business clothes or security uniforms. Luna Layla directs them to the sitting room while I quietly bring in pitchers of water and ice tea for them to drink. I do my best to try not to be noticed when one of the women calls me out. "You there, omega," She says abruptly. I look around and realize she is speaking to me. " For everyone." "Maya, of course, right away," Luna Layla says quickly, then nods her head to me. I rush to the cellar and pull out two cases of napkins, and glasses, prepping the drink service cart and head back to the sitting room. I open three bottles, leaving the rest for them to do as they wish and I back out of the room so I can start preparing dinner. The rest of the day goes without a hitch. The guests seem pleased with dinner. In the evening, I go to each guest suite to make sure everyone is happy with their accommodations. A couple of people ask for more bags of chips or soda but on the whole, everyone seems satisfied. The last door is the Beta's room. Maya opens the door, looking much more relaxed than earlier. She has a large tattoo of a rose and a dagger on her forearm. Her dark hair is still pulled back but she isn't wearing makeup. I can see now, she looks only a few years older than me. I can hear her mate inside talking on the phone. "Thanks for checking on us. Everything is wonderful. The flowers are a beautiful touch. You have good taste," she smiles at me. I bow to her slightly, then turn to leave. "Wait, what's under your hat?" I stop in my tracks and turn around. "I'm sorry ma'am?" I ask. I feel the blood drain from my face. "Your hat. Why is it so low? What are you trying to hide?" she asks, "Come closer." I come closer and slowly take off my hat. Keeping my eyes to the ground. My silver hair cascades down my back. It is embarrassingly greasy and visibly dirty. I feel myself blush. "Oh, I see," she says with surprise in her voice, "Now. Don't be disrespectful. Always look me in the eye when I speak to you." I look up at her. The light from her room shines right into my eyes. She looks at me blankly for a moment trying to process what she is seeing. "What are you? A hybrid?" "No, ma'am. The pack doctor did tests but doesn't know why it happened. He thinks it must be a transformation related to my wolf getting ready to wake up," I mean, it's not a lie...it's just not the whole truth, right? How am I supposed to tell a stranger that my wolf says I am the Moon Goddess's actual daughter and that is why I have silver hair and violet eyes? She grabs my chin and pulls my face closer to hers, inspecting closely, "And does the pack doctor know someone has broken your nose recently? You still have bruises." "He's treated my injuries in the past," I'm not trying to elaborate or implicate anyone to this person I don’t know. "Who's at the door, Maya?" the Beta inside calls to her. "Just the omega assigned to us, Caden. What's your name, again?" "It's Talia, ma'am but please call me Talia. I'm not an omega, though. I'm just a servant." "Her name is Talia. She picked out my beautiful flowers," she's still talking to her mate but she hasn't taken her eyes off me as if she is trying to size me up for some reason. Her brow furrows slightly as she stares. She's making me self-conscious. "That's nice. Ask her if I can get bubbly water in the refrigerator." "No problem, ma'am," She and I share a smile at 'bubbly water', "I will bring it shortly and leave it at the door.” "Thank you. Oh and Talia, if those bruises aren't healed tomorrow morning, find some powder. Alpha Damon does not tolerate seeing injuries like that." "Ye-yes, ma'am." I run to the stockroom, get four bottles of San Pellegrino, and put them in front of the door, then run away as fast as I can. One million questions run through my head. Would their Alpha be angry for being weaker than other wolves even if I was not part of his pack? Was she going to tell Alpha Edward about my unusual features? Was she going to call him out for letting someone break my nose? I mean, lady, if you think that is bad, I got some news you're not gonna like and then I'm dead meat by your Alpha for sure. Alpha Edward comes down later and whips me for not having all the items our guests wanted. By morning, Sylvie has still not been able to fully heal me. I’m in so much pain, everything is a struggle. Cooking, carrying breakfast trays, leaning over to clean tables. Every move causes scabs to open and bleed, making the back of my shirt damp with blood. Maya makes eye contact with me a couple of times. She can tell something was wrong but doesn't say anything. For some reason she can't explain, Sylvie is bouncing around in my head all morning. “The Beta is so nice! I can't wait to meet the Alpha and Luna!” “Sylvie , come on. We're not going to get to meet the Alpha and Luna. We're going to melt into the wallpaper and pretend we don't exist.” “I want to meet them.” “Okay, well I hate to disappoint you, but you're gonna get disappointed.” Layla comes in while I'm prepping lunch to let me know the Alpha has arrived and I need to make lunch for him as well. There is no Luna. He doesn't have a mate? And according to Layla...he's handsome. Not that it matters to me, because I'm going to be wallpaper. I don't want him to notice me at all. I take the trays to the conference room. Alpha Damon is not there but there is a spot at the table where he is supposed to sit. I leave his meal at the empty seat. Everyone from the Dark Howlers Pack politely thanks me as I lay plates in front of them. Their manners betray their intimidating features. No one from the Red Moon pack says a word to me as I serve them. I collect the trays and walk out quietly. Layla lets me know she will clean the plates so I can focus on dinner and food for the party. I go to the kitchen but need a minute to collect myself before I get started on dinner. I go out the back door and stand on the stoop. In the distance, I don't recognize him, it must be the Alpha from Dark Howlers. He is too far away for me to see his actual features though. All I can see is a tall figure with dark hair and a suit. It smells like but I swear it smells like coffee too...or dark chocolate. This guy was a mocha drinker? I laugh to myself at the thought of the big bad Alpha of Dark Howlers sipping on a mochaccino. I make a four-course meal of Caesar salad, bacon-wrapped shrimp appetizers, beef wellington with braised Brussels sprouts for the main dish, and a key lime pie for dessert. I also make bruschetta, tomato fritters, mini calzones, assorted veggie trays with dip, and chocolate truffles to serve for the party. I finished the desserts and veggie trays between breakfast and lunch so there was less for me to worry about now. I realize Sylvie 's advice of finding happiness in cooking has helped me enjoy making this dinner. Maybe because I'm serving people other than my pack or maybe it's because I'm making special food, not just the regular stuff I make for the pack? Either way, I don't mind my work today. I felt a sense of pride in it. There are servers for dinner service since it's a formal event. I stay in the kitchen and make sure everything is plated and going out the door in perfect condition. I'm in the zone, as they say. I peek out from the kitchen after each course is served. People seem to enjoy the food, which is a relief. I notice Alpha Edward is getting pretty drunk. Luna Layla keeps taking his glass away from him, but he keeps ordering the omegas to give him more. The dining room is extra crowded, so I don't get a better look at Alpha Damon. Maya sees me peeking out from the kitchen and gives me a wink and thumbs up. I smile and give a little wave before pulling my head back. I help the servers take the party food to the tables at the edges of the ballroom. I also make sure the bars in the corners are fully stocked. The DJ is finishing setting up and colorful lights are sliding across the floor. Party balloons and streamers are hanging all over the place. The first few guests are starting to wander in which is my cue to duck out the back door. Luckily, the dinner servers will clean up the dinner service tonight, which gives me extra time to restock pantries. I head upstairs to the stockroom and load the cart up. I'm humming to myself as I go from room to room. I feel an odd sense of calm as I go. "You're in a good mood," Sylvie  says. "I guess. I'm not sure why though. My back and feet still make me feel bad. " "Well, I'm happy that you're happy for once. This version of you is pretty cool." "Thanks,  Sylvie . You're not half bad yourself." I finish stocking the ranked pack members' rooms on the fourth and third floors. Then head to the second floor where the guest suites are. The cleaning staff has cleaned the rooms and bathrooms. I just need to restock the toiletries, pantry items, and refrigerators. I make quick work of the rooms. I remember to stock the Betas' room with more bottles of San Pellegrino, refresh the flowers, and leave a little tent card with a handwritten smiley face on the kitchenette counter. 

It was almost midnight by the time I was wrapping up, and everyone was still in the ballroom. 

I closed the door to the Beta's suite and moved on to the Alpha's suite door. 

It's the last room left. He must be at the party too, but I knocked before entering just in case.

I put my ear against the door and heard nothing, so I slipped my key in the lock and opened the door, but the moment I looked inside, my heart stopped, and I froze. 

Standing there was the most handsome werewolf I've ever seen in my life.

Easily six foot, six inches tall, looked to be about two hundred fifty pounds of solid muscle with the broadest shoulders, but he wasn’t alone, an icy Blonde stood in front of him with her hands undoing his belt.

The smell of coffee and dark chocolate filled the air, and my mind went hazy as I froze, seeing two piercing blue eyes staring back at me. 

"Stop!" He shouted.

'Is this it? Is this the day I die?' I wondered.

I was only doing my job, but that did not change the fact that I had witnessed something that should not have been seen.

Before I could move, he lunged forward and roughly pinned me against the floor outside the room with a low growl. 

He placed both hands on my shoulders, preventing me from escaping, put his face against my neck, and inhaled deeply. My heart was pounding in my chest as overwhelming panic began to set in.

“Alpha Damon, is this Omega trying to steal something?” A guard said, seeing the struggle. 

“Get back.” He snarled, flashing his large fangs.

“Mine,” he growled. 

Over his shoulder, I could faintly see Marcy staring daggers at me, and down the hall, I heard Alpha Edward shouting. 

‘What a disaster’ I thought, ‘they’re all going to kill me.’

My head started swimming, and I felt even dizzier, maybe I was finally dying. 

“Look what, you’ve done you little bitch!” 

Marcy yelled as she reached out to grab me, but she never touched me, Alpha Damon snarled, snatching her hand out of the air and snapping her wrist. 

Alpha Edward roared, “How dare you! This is war!”

I watched them fight as if it was a dream. They looked as though they were moving in slow motion. 

Alpha Edward yanked Marcy, pulling her back as Damon snarled at them, he was vicious, beautifully vicious.

A guard tried to separate them as Beta Caden and Maya took defensive positions around Alpha Damon, and George lunged at Damon, but he was no match for the Alpha.

Damon grabbed George by the throat and threw him into the wall as though her were a tiny pup.

I almost laughed, but I was shaking all over, barely able to stand, but in the chaos, I managed to crawl away and slink down the stairs. 

I looked around to see if anyone noticed me, but they were all too busy arguing.

I looked down to see blood running down my legs, dripping onto the floor. I started to lose consciousness, and then I heard it, the most guttural, ear-shattering roar.

“WHERE IS SHE?!”

“Where is who, Alpha Damon?”

“WHERE IS MY MATE?!”

Is it possible?
Is Talia truly Damon’s fated mate?
What will Damon do to protect her?
Will their bond ignite a war between the two most powerful packs in the order?
Will any of them leave Red Moon territory alive?

A high school project humbled me today
My 16-year-old just texted me a screenshot and I don't know whether to be proud or humiliated.

She got her learner's permit three weeks ago. Hasn't driven on a real road yet. Still parks like she's defusing a bomb.

But for some school project on "adulting," her teacher had them pull a quote on what it would cost to insure their own hypothetical car. A used 2018 Civic. Just to see.

She sent me the number. $89 a month.

I'm 43. Clean record. Drive a 2019 Accord. I pay $237.

I asked her how she got that number. She said the teacher gave them a site to use — some quiz thing. Took her like two minutes during 4th period.

So I sat in my driveway after work and did the same thing. Same site she used. Honest answers. My car, my zip, my actual record.

$47 a month.

I've been with the same company since I bought my first truck in 2007. Eighteen years of on-time payments, no accidents, no tickets. And a kid who's never legally driven a car just out-shopped me in a high school classroom on her lunch break.

She asked me at dinner if I was going to switch. I told her I already did it on my phone before she got home.

She just looked at me and goes, "Dad. I'm 16. You're supposed to be teaching me this stuff."

Fair.

The site her teacher gave them is below if you want to feel the same way I felt sitting in that driveway.

https://autoratesnow.com/form/

BOTOX® Cosmetic (onabotulinumtoxinA) is a prescription medicine that is injected into muscles and used to temporarily improve the look of moderate to severe forehead lines, crow's feet, and frown lines between the eyebrows in adults.
-
Talk to your doctor about BOTOX® Cosmetic and whether it’s right for you. There are risks with this product—the effects of BOTOX® Cosmetic may spread hours to weeks after injection causing serious symptoms. Alert your doctor right away as difficulty swallowing, speaking, breathing, eye problems or muscle weakness can be a sign of a life-threatening condition. If this happens, do not drive a car, operate machinery, or do other dangerous activities. Patients with these conditions before injection are at the highest risk. Swallowing problems may last for several months. Side effects may include allergic reactions, neck and injection-site pain, fatigue and headache. Allergic reactions can include rash, welts, asthma symptoms, and dizziness. Don’t receive BOTOX® Cosmetic if there’s a skin infection. Tell your doctor your medical history, muscle or nerve conditions (including ALS/Lou Gehrig's disease, myasthenia gravis, or Lambert-Eaton syndrome), and medications, including botulinum toxins, as these may increase the risk of serious side effects.
-

@breyers CarbSmart Vanilla has entered the chat 🍦🍫👩🏼‍🍳 #BreyersPartner #Breyers recipe below!

@breyers CarbSmart Vanilla has only 100 calories and 4g of sugar per serving, and it’s truly SO creamy and delicious. It perfectly pairs with my low carb brownies 

what you’ll need:
Breyers CarbSmart Vanilla 
2 eggs
1/2 cup Greek yogurt 
1/2 cup peanut butter (or other nut butter)
1/3 cup maple syrup
1 tsp vanilla extract
1/2 cup chocolate or unflavored protein powder
1/3 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
1/4 cup almond flour or oat flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/4 cup unsweetened dark chocolate chips (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line an 8×8-inch baking pan with parchment paper and set aside.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, Greek yogurt, nut butter, maple syrup, and vanilla until smooth and well combined.
3. Add the cocoa powder, protein powder, almond flour, baking powder, and salt. Stir until a thick, fully mixed batter forms.
4. If using, gently fold in the dark chocolate chips.
5. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread it evenly.
6. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with moist crumbs. Be careful not to overbake, these are best when fudgy.
7. Let the brownies cool completely in the pan before slicing into squares.
8. Top with a scoop of Breyers CarbSmart Vanilla and enjoy!
templates.example_product_desc: A low-calorie, low-sugar vanilla ice cream from Breyers (about 100 calories and 4 g sugar per serving).

BOTOX® Cosmetic (onabotulinumtoxinA) is a prescription medicine that is injected into muscles and used to temporarily improve the look of moderate to severe forehead lines, crow's feet, and frown lines between the eyebrows in adults. 
-
Talk to your doctor about BOTOX® Cosmetic and whether it’s right for you. There are risks with this product—the effects of BOTOX® Cosmetic may spread hours to weeks after injection causing serious symptoms. Alert your doctor right away as difficulty swallowing, speaking, breathing, eye problems or muscle weakness can be a sign of a life-threatening condition. If this happens, do not drive a car, operate machinery, or do other dangerous activities. Patients with these conditions before injection are at the highest risk. Swallowing problems may last for several months. Side effects may include allergic reactions, neck and injection-site pain, fatigue and headache. Don’t receive BOTOX® Cosmetic if there’s a skin infection. Tell your doctor your medical history, muscle or nerve conditions, and medications, including botulinum toxins, as these may increase the risk of serious side effects.
_
Intended for U.S. audiences only.

Why your electric bill is high — even when you're barely home
Your phone charger runs on DC power.

Your laptop? DC. Your TV? DC. Your LED lights? DC.

But your home is still delivering AC — the same electrical system from 140 years ago.

So every single device in your house has to convert that power before using it.

And every time it converts?

Energy leaks out as heat.

That adapter getting warm on your laptop charger?

That's called Dirty Electricity.

And according to researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, it's responsible for nearly half of what you pay every month.

Not because you're using too much.

Because your home is wasting power before your devices can even touch it.

A 30-year electrician just released a video explaining exactly how this works — and what you can do about it starting today.

→ Watch the full explanation here

When Andy was diagnosed with RMS, he was overwhelmed. His neurologist prescribed KESIMPTA® (ofatumumab) as his first-line treatment. Now, he can experience the power of the pen,* with the average injection time being 3–4 seconds when ready.1,2†

With efficacy data and an easy-to-use pen,3-5‡ you can feel more confident making KESIMPTA your first choice—and you can start your patients today with samples.§

*As evidenced by reduction in ARR, MRI (Gd+ T1 and T2 lesions), and 3- and 6-month CDP vs teriflunomide. Primary end point, ARR reduction of 51% (0.11 vs 0.22), 58% (0.10 vs 0.25).1,6

†As per stability technical specification data, when the patient is ready to inject, it typically takes an average of 3-4 seconds a month to administer. Once-monthly dosing begins after the initial dosing period, which consists of 20-mg SC doses at weeks 0, 1, and 2. Please see Instructions for Use for more detailed instructions on preparation and administration of KESIMPTA.1,2

‡Based on a survey of adult RMS patients (N=105) in
the US who self-administered KESIMPTA within the
previous year. 89.5% of patients scored a 4 or 5 on ease of use. Questionnaire has not been validated. Initiation of KESIMPTA in patients may be influenced by insurance and availability (among other issues). Hence, data should be cautiously interpreted.4,5

Patients were randomized to double-dummy SC KESIMPTA (20 mg every 4 weeks) or oral Aubagio® (teriflunomide) (14 mg daily) for up to 30 months. Primary end point was ARR. Key secondary end points were number of Gd+ T1 lesions and annualized rate of NE T2 lesions, and reduction in risk of 3-month CDP. Treatment duration was variable based on end-of-study criteria. Maximum duration: 120 weeks; median duration: 85 weeks.1

ARR, annualized relapse rate; CDP, confirmed disability progression; DMT, disease-modifying therapy; Gd+, gadolinium-enhancing; MRI, magnetic resonance imaging; NE, new or enlarging; RMS, relapsing multiple sclerosis; SC, subcutaneous.

Spend a day in the life with Taylor to discover what inspired her personal BOTOX® Cosmetic journey and how it has inspired others.

Find a licensed specialist to see if BOTOX® Cosmetic is right for you!
-
BOTOX® Cosmetic (onabotulinumtoxinA) is a prescription medicine that is injected into muscles and used to temporarily improve the look of moderate to severe forehead lines, crow's feet, and frown lines between the eyebrows in adults.
-
Talk to your doctor about BOTOX® Cosmetic and whether it’s right for you. There are risks with this product—the effects of BOTOX® Cosmetic may spread hours to weeks after injection causing serious symptoms. Alert your doctor right away as difficulty swallowing, speaking, breathing, eye problems or muscle weakness can be a sign of a life-threatening condition. If this happens, do not drive a car, operate machinery, or do other dangerous activities. Patients with these conditions before injection are at the highest risk. Swallowing problems may last for several months. Side effects may include allergic reactions, neck and injection-site pain, fatigue and headache. Allergic reactions can include rash, welts, asthma symptoms, and dizziness. Don’t receive BOTOX® Cosmetic if there’s a skin infection. Tell your doctor your medical history, muscle or nerve conditions (including ALS/Lou Gehrig's disease, myasthenia gravis, or Lambert-Eaton syndrome), and medications, including botulinum toxins, as these may increase the risk of serious side effects.
-
Intended for U.S. audiences only.
BOTOX® Cosmetic

Why your electric bill is high — even when you're barely home
Most people don’t realize this.

Your phone, TV, laptop — almost everything you use runs on DC power.

But your home still receives AC electricity…
a system designed over a century ago.

So before your devices can even work, they have to convert that power.

And during that conversion?

A portion of the energy is lost as heat.

That’s why your chargers get warm.
That heat is wasted electricity.

Now imagine that happening across your entire house… all day long.

Researchers have found this waste can make up a large part of your monthly bill.

Not because you’re using more.
Because you’re losing energy before it’s even used.

A veteran electrician recently explained this in a simple way.

→ Watch the explanation here

You Deserve To Be Happy Again. ☺️
I used to rewrite emails seven times before hitting send. You know that feeling, right? When you've crafted the "perfect" response, but then you read it again and suddenly it sounds too casual. So you rewrite it. Then it sounds too formal. Rewrite again. Now it's too long. Delete half of it. Wait, now it doesn't make sense. Start over.

Twenty minutes later, you're sending a two-sentence email that you've agonized over like it was going to be published in the Sunday paper.

That was me with everything. The perfect Instagram caption that took an hour to write. The "casual" outfit that required trying on twelve different combinations. The text message I'd type and delete seventeen times before just... not sending it at all.

Perfectionism has this sneaky way of disguising itself as high standards, doesn't it? It whispers that you're just being thorough, just caring about quality, just wanting to do your best. But really? It's fear wearing a fancy mask.

That's exactly why this interactive bracelet has become my daily reality check. The moment I catch myself spiraling into that familiar "it's not good enough" loop, I tap my phone to my wrist. Instantly, an affirmation appears that meets me right in that perfectionist panic.

Sometimes it's "Done is better than perfect." Other times it might be "Your worth isn't measured by your mistakes." The app somehow knows exactly what I need to hear when my inner perfectionist starts running the show.

It's like having a wise friend right there with you, ready to remind you that progress beats perfection every single time. Someone who remembers that the goal isn't to be flawless - it's to keep moving forward, even when forward feels messy.

Because here's what perfectionism doesn't want you to know: every single thing you admire was created by someone who decided that "good enough to share" was better than "perfect but hidden." Every book, every song, every piece of art that's ever moved you - none of it was perfect. But all of it was brave enough to exist.

If someone depends on your income, you need term life insurance. Period.

I’ve said it for decades, and I’ll keep saying it: Life insurance isn’t about you. It’s about protecting the people you love.

If you died tomorrow, how would your family keep the lights on? Pay the mortgage? Afford groceries?

That’s where term life insurance steps in. It replaces your income so your family can stay afloat during the worst-case scenario. It’s not flashy, but it’s essential.

And this isn’t just for parents working outside of the house. If you’re a stay-at-home parent, you need life insurance too.

Think about everything you do in a day: child care, cleaning, cooking, transportation. If something happened to you, your spouse would need to pay for all those services—and that adds up fast. Term life coverage can make sure your family has the help they need to keep going.

Don’t fall for the whole life insurance scams. They cost more and cover less. And they’re stuffed with gimmicks that make insurance companies rich, not you.

Term life insurance is simple, affordable, and does exactly what you need it to do: cover your family while they still depend on you.

I recommend a 15- or 20-year term policy worth 10–12 times your annual income. That way, your family could invest the payout and live off the growth without touching the principal.

It takes less than five minutes to find out what it would cost you. Use this free tool to get your personalized estimate: https://ter.li/Term_Life_Estimate

Protect your family. Sleep better tonight.

Why everyone fatigued should be grounding
I'm going to sound crazy, but hear me out.

(Anyone struggling with fatigue or low energy, this is for you.)

Until 2 weeks ago, I was waking up exhausted EVERY morning. Didn't matter if I slept 4 hours or 8 hours, I'd wake up feeling like I didn’t sleep at all. By noon I'd already be drained, brain fog so bad I couldn’t focus on anything. Couldn't remember the last time I felt like myself. I felt tired and annoyed all the time.

I'd tried everything. Blackout curtains. Supplement after supplement. From drinking 5 coffees a day just to function to quitting coffee completely to see if that would help. I even tried going on a gluten-free diet. But basically nothing I tried did anything. 

Then I saw this article pop up on Facebook written by a rheumatologist from New York. I almost scrolled past it but the headline was something about fatigue not just being about sleep and I was like... Wait what?

Read the whole thing. He was talking about how there's this deeper issue people don't talk enough about that makes the symptoms so much worse. He mentioned grounding therapy and that these grounding sheets can be helpful to bring back energy levels naturally.

(I don't remember the exact details, if you're curious just read the article I've linked below.)

Anyways, I was obviously skeptical. But at that point I'd already wasted money on everything else that didn't work, and this had a 90-day money-back guarantee so I figured why not. They seemed confident, and there was literally nothing to lose because I would just return it if it didn't work.

Got the sheet, plugged it in, went to sleep thinking "this is ridiculous." I even laughed at myself for even trying something like this.

But the next morning as I was brushing my teeth, I realized that I’d slept through the ENTIRE night - for NINE HOURS. And for the first time in I don't even know how long, I wasn't thinking about being tired and what I should do to not feel tired. If you struggle with fatigue, you know exactly what I’m talking about.

The next morning I woke up and actually felt... refreshed? My husband looked at me like "How long have you been awake?" because apparently I didn’t look as tired. But I only woke up a couple of minutes before him.

Two weeks in - I feel 10 years younger. The midday crashes are basically gone. I only have one cup of coffee in the morning, and I still sleep better than I have in years. Brain fog seems to have gone down too. I can’t describe it but my mind feels more clear.

And I haven't bitten anyone's head off in a while (my husband loves it too).

I know this might sound crazy but I figured if it helped me, maybe it can also help other ladies out there going through this nightmare of feeling tired 24/7.

If you’re interested here’s the link to the article:

https://journal.groundingwell.com/pages/o4
Greatest Health Rediscovery

How to Choose Nonconventional Lodging Over a Hotel for Your TDY Assignment
When preparing for a Temporary Duty (TDY) assignment, selecting the right lodging is a crucial decision that can significantly impact your overall experience. While hotels have long been the standard choice, short-term rentals (STRs) are increasingly becoming the preferred option for military personnel. STRs offer numerous benefits, from enhanced privacy to cost savings, but understanding the process to secure one can be the key to making this transition seamless. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you navigate the process of choosing a short-term rental over a hotel for your next TDY assignment.

Step 1: Submit an Initial Request for Reservation
The process begins with submitting an initial request for your TDY lodging. At 9 Line Agency, we make this step as straightforward as possible. You’ll need to provide essential details, including the number of people traveling, the duration of the stay, and the desired location. This information allows us to tailor our offerings to your specific needs, ensuring that we can find the perfect accommodations for your assignment.

Step 2: Pre-Emptive Planning and Exploring Options
Once we receive your request, our team at 9 Line Agency will engage in pre-emptive planning. We understand that the military’s needs can vary greatly, so we provide a range of options that showcase our capability to accommodate different group sizes and requirements. Whether you’re booking for one person or an entire unit, we’ll present you with multiple choices, each designed to support your mission effectively. This step is crucial in demonstrating how STRs can offer superior value compared to traditional hotels.

Step 3: Secure Final Approval from Your Unit
Before finalizing any lodging arrangements, it’s essential to obtain approval from your unit. This step ensures that your chosen accommodations align with military standards and mission requirements. At this stage, your unit will review the options provided and make a decision based on what best suits the operational needs. Having a variety of STR options available can make it easier to secure this approval, as they often provide more flexibility and comfort compared to standard hotel rooms. This step may include 9 Line Agency sharing the approved memos for your unit to approve prior to traveling, helping to get Non-A letters if applicable and much more depending on your unit's needs. 

Step 4: Reserve and Secure Your Short-Term Rental
Once your unit has approved the STR option, the next step is to reserve and secure the appropriate number of rentals to support the mission. At 9 Line Agency, we handle this process for you, ensuring that all details are confirmed well in advance. This includes securing multiple properties in close proximity if necessary, or setting up a “planning house” to serve as a central hub for your team. Our goal is to make sure that all logistics are taken care of so that you can focus on your mission.

Step 5: Receive Final Invoices and Prepare for Your Stay
Approximately 30 days before your scheduled arrival, we’ll send you the final invoices. This step allows for any necessary financial arrangements to be made well ahead of time, ensuring there are no surprises upon arrival. With everything confirmed, you can focus on preparing for your assignment, knowing that your lodging is secured and ready.

Step 6: Check-In and Enjoy a Smooth Stay
Finally, two days before your arrival, we’ll provide you with detailed check-in procedures. At 9 Line Agency, we understand the importance of a seamless experience, so we also monitor your trip to ensure everything goes as planned. Our team is on hand to address any issues that may arise, ensuring that your stay is as comfortable and efficient as possible.

Why Choose a Short-Term Rental (Nonconventional Lodging) Over a Hotel?

Opting for a short-term rental over a hotel offers numerous advantages for military personnel on TDY assignments. STRs provide enhanced privacy, with more space for planning and relaxation. They also feature fully equipped kitchens, promoting healthier living and camaraderie among your team. Additionally, STRs often result in significant cost savings, allowing you to stay within your per diem while enjoying a superior lodging experience.
By following this straightforward process, you can easily secure a short-term rental that not only meets but exceeds the standards of traditional hotel accommodations. At 9 Line Agency, we are dedicated to making your TDY experience as smooth and successful as possible, ensuring that your lodging supports your mission every step of the way.

The weirdest "thank you" I've ever received (it happened at 30,000 feet)
Red-eye flight to Boston. I'm in seat 32B. The one that doesn't recline next to the bathroom.
I'm wearing my DearPersonCo hoodie because it's cozy and flights are freezing.
About an hour in, flight attendant taps my shoulder.
"Ma'am, would you please come with me?"
I'm thinking I'm in trouble. Did I accidentally take someone's seat? Is my bag too big?
She walks me to first class. Points to seat 2A.
"This gentleman would like to speak with you."
Guy in a full suit, working on a laptop.
He goes: "I walked past you during boarding. Read the message on your hoodie."
"Dear person behind me, the world is a better place with you in it."
He paused.
"My daughter's been struggling. I've been so focused on work I haven't been present. Your hoodie reminded me what matters."
Then he says: "I'd like to swap seats with you for the rest of the flight. You should be comfortable while wearing a message like that."
I tried to say no. He insisted.
We swapped.
I spent the rest of the flight in first class because of a simple hoodie.
Before we landed, he showed me his phone. He'd sent her a message: "I'm sorry I haven't been there. I love you. Call me when you wake up."
But here's what got me thinking.
What if I wore something else that day?
What if he never looked up from his laptop?
What if his daughter never got that message?
That was eight months ago.
Since then, it's happened three more times.
A barista at Starbucks. Wrote "thank you" on my cup and said she'd been having the worst week.
A woman at Target. Tapped my shoulder in the checkout line. She just said "thank you for wearing that" and walked away.
A man at my son's soccer game. Walked up to me after and said, "I needed to see that today. More than you know."
Different people. Different places. Same thing.
And here's why I'm telling you this.
I didn't have to say anything. I didn't have to do anything. I just wore it.

Why every menopausal woman should be grounding
"Are you seeing someone?" That's what my husband asked me last Tuesday. Dead serious.

The night sweats meant I was up at 2am every night, which meant he was up too. I'd have to change my pajamas, sometimes even put a towel down on the sheets. We were both exhausted.

I stayed silent.

"You seem to be in a brighter mood nowadays," with a suspicious look on his face.

"Yeah."

He didn't say anything else. Just went back to his coffee.

Then I started noticing him doing strange things — things he hadn’t done in a while. He'd ask me about my day and actually listen to my answer. He'd make the bed in the morning, which he never did. Slowly but surely, we were talking again.

I didn't think much of it. 

But it kept happening. Every few nights, I'd wake up and he'd be on my side of the bed.

Then one Saturday morning, I got up early to make coffee. When I came back upstairs, he was awake, sitting on the edge of the bed.

"I need to tell you something," he said.

"What is it?"

"I think there’s something to the sheets you got."

“What do you mean?” I said.

"To be honest my back has been killing me for a while. I didn’t want to tell you because you were dealing with enough. But I could barely sleep. And then I noticed when I accidentally rolled onto your side one night, I ended up sleeping through the night. Didn’t have the aches in the morning, either."

"So you've been sleeping on the grounding sheet." I said, with the I-told-you-so look.

He looked at me. "I guess there’s something to it. I'm sorry I gave you a hard time about buying it. I wouldn’t mind you putting it across the bed."

Last week, we were at dinner with our friends. 

Our friend Kate, who’s also going through menopause, was talking about her experience—night sweats, exhaustion, mood swings. All of it.

After I stopped crying, he said: "The past couple of years, it felt like you were here but never actually here. And then a few weeks ago, all the sudden you came back and seemed happier. I didn't know what changed, I just knew you were different, and just thought maybe…"

“No, of course not,” I said. 

"I'm actually sleeping properly for the first time in a long time. I have the energy to do things, and everything else feels better. That’s what’s changed."

"It's not just that. You're you again. We're us again."

He was right. We'd gone from barely speaking to actually talking every day. From sleeping on opposite sides of the bed to waking up next to each other. From existing together to actually being married again.

A bedsheet didn't save my marriage. But it gave me enough sleep and enough energy to show up as myself again. And that changed everything.

The man who built our deck with his bare hands.
The man who carried our daughter on his shoulders at Disney World for four hours straight without breaking a sweat.
Now, he was sobbing. Quietly, trying not to wake me up.
But I was awake. I’m always awake when the "fire" starts.
I walked over and knelt beside him. His feet were glowing red, hot to the touch, swollen and angry.
"I can't do this anymore, Sarah," he whispered, his voice cracking. "It feels like I'm walking on hot coals. Just cut them off. I’m serious. I’d rather have no feet than feel this."
That was the moment I stopped trusting what we had been told.
For three years, we had played the "good patient" game.
We went to the specialist who looked at his chart for thirty seconds, didn't even look at his feet, and scribbled a prescription.
"Take these," he said. "It's the standard protocol."
So Mark took them.
And I watched my husband slowly disappear.
The pills turned him into a zombie.
He couldn't remember words. He would stop mid-sentence and just stare at the wall. He was dizzy all the time, stumbling around the kitchen like he’d had three beers before breakfast.
"I hate this," he told me once, staring at the little orange bottle. "I feel like my brain is wrapped in cotton."
But the worst part? The pain was still there.
It just... moved further away. He was too drugged to care as much, but his body still knew.
He still kicked the sheets off every night.
He still winced if the dog brushed against his leg.
So we tried the creams. God, we tried everything.
Our bathroom cabinet became a graveyard of half-used tubes.
Menthol gels that smelled so strong our eyes watered.
Lidocaine patches that rolled off in the middle of the night.
Expensive oils I ordered from a late-night infomercial that stained our expensive sheets and made the whole bedroom smell like a metaphysical shop.
They all did the same thing:
They burned or froze his skin for about twenty minutes.
It was a distraction. It wasn't relief.
It was like shouting at a screaming baby to drown out the noise, instead of checking to see if the baby was hungry.
That night in the living room, watching him rock back and forth, I realized we were losing.
If we kept doing this—the pills, the burning creams, the sleepless nights—he was going to give up.
I made him a cup of tea, got him settled with an ice pack (which barely helped), and I opened my laptop.
I didn't go to the forums this time. I was sick of reading other people’s misery.
I started digging into medical journals. Old ones. New ones. I wanted to understand the mechanics of what was happening inside his legs.
I searched until my eyes blurred. 3 AM. 4 AM.
And then, I found a lecture transcript from a retired neurologist that stopped me cold.
He wasn't talking about "pain management." He was talking about starvation.
He explained that the "burning" sensation isn't just a random signal.
It’s a distress signal.
He compared the nerves in the feet to a dying battery.
When the small blood vessels in the legs shrink (from age, or blood sugar issues, or toxins), the nerves stop getting the nutrients they need.
They start to wither.
And when a nerve is damaged and starving, it doesn't just shut off. It misfires.
It sends frantic, chaotic signals to the brain.
Heat. Electric shocks. Pins and needles. Ants crawling.
It's the nerve screaming for help.
And here was the kicker:
Most "pain relief" creams on the market use Counter-Irritants.
Menthol, Camphor, Capsaicin.
They work by irritating the skin on purpose. They create a sensation of "burning" or "freezing" on the surface to trick the brain into ignoring the deeper pain.
They are literally designed to distract you.
They don't feed the nerve. They don't calm the signal. They just create a louder noise.
I looked over at Mark, finally dozing off in the chair, his feet still red.
We had been trying to scream over the pain with menthol.
We had been trying to numb the brain with pills so it couldn't hear the screams.
But nobody had tried to just... feed the nerves.
Nobody had tried to calm the storm at the source.
I felt a mix of rage and hope.
Why hadn't the doctor told us this? Why was the answer "numb it" instead of "nourish it"?
I started searching for something different.
I didn't want a "pain blocker." I wanted something that absorbed.
I learned that the skin on the feet is tough. It’s designed to keep things out.
Most lotions sit on top. They’re greasy because the molecules are too big to get through the protective barrier. They just hydrate the dead skin cells on the surface.
I needed something with a delivery system. Something that could actually penetrate deep enough to reach those screaming nerve endings.
I found a small company called Mama Bear.
I almost scrolled past them. The name sounded cute, not clinical.
But then I read the reviews.
They weren't just saying "good product."
They were telling my story.
"I got off Gabapentin."
"I can finally sleep with the sheets touching my feet."
"The fire is gone."
It wasn't a "heat rub." It didn't rely on burning the skin to work.
It used a specific formulation of Magnesium and natural calmers, but the secret was how they blended it.
They called it "deep-dive" absorption.
It wasn't designed to sit on the skin. It was designed to vanish into it. To reach the nerves that were misfiring and settle them down.
I ordered a jar.
I didn't tell Mark. I didn't want to get his hopes up again.
When it arrived three days later, I waited until evening.
He was sitting on the edge of the bed, doing his nightly ritual—rubbing his calves, dreading the moment he had to lie down.
"Just try this," I said, handing him the white jar.
He looked at me with that tired, skeptical look. The look that said, Another one?
"It doesn't smell like a nursing home," I promised. "And it's not going to burn."
He opened it. It had a light, clean scent. Like a spa, not a locker room.
He took a scoop and rubbed it onto his left foot.
"It's gone," he said.
"What's gone?"
"The cream. It's already dry."
He was right. No grease. No sticky residue. His skin just drank it in like it was dying of thirst.
He did the other foot.
We sat there for a minute.
"Well," he sighed. "Feels okay. Let's see."
He laid back.
Usually, within ten minutes of lying horizontal, the "zaps" start. The electric shocks that make his whole leg jump.
I laid next to him, reading a book, waiting for the flinch.
Ten minutes passed.
Twenty.
I looked over. His breathing had evened out. His eyes were closed.
He wasn't twitching. He wasn't kicking the covers off.
I turned off the lamp and lay in the dark, listening.
For the first time in years, I didn't hear him whimpering in his sleep.
I fell asleep holding my breath, terrified I would jinx it.
I woke up at 6:30 AM.
The sun was coming through the blinds.
Mark was still asleep.
But that wasn't what made me start crying.
It was the sheets.
The duvet was pulled up over his feet.
For three years, he has slept with his feet sticking out because the weight of the fabric felt like "broken glass."
But there they were. Tucked in. Comfortable. Quiet.
He woke up about ten minutes later and looked at the clock. Panic flashed across his face.
"I slept," he said, sounding confused. "I slept the whole night."
He wiggled his toes.
"It’s not burning, Sarah. It’s... quiet."
That was three weeks ago.
He hasn't taken a "zombie pill" in 14 days.
He’s walking the dog again.
Yesterday, I saw him standing in the kitchen, drinking coffee, and he was dancing a little bit to the radio.
He wasn't leaning on the counter to take the weight off his feet.
I'm sharing this because I know there are thousands of people staring at the ceiling right now.
I know you're tired.
I know you're skeptical because you've been burned (literally) by products that didn't work.
But you have to understand:
Your nerves aren't just "in pain." They are starving.
Stop trying to distract them with burning creams.
Stop trying to silence them with heavy drugs that steal your life away.
You need to feed them. You need to calm them.
This white jar isn't magic. It's just... correct.
It understands the problem in a way my doctor didn't.
If you are dreading bedtime tonight...
If you are terrified of the "3 AM scream"...
If you just want to feel the sheets on your toes again without wincing...
You need to try Mama Bear Oasis.
Mark calls it his "off switch." I call it the reason I got my husband back.
Don't spend another night in the chair.
Click below to see if it can help you finally sleep.

templates.example_body:
Every Parent Needs This!
I'm the mom who didn't check until it was too late. Three hotels, three cameras, all recording my daughter.

This was supposed to be Emma's perfect thirteenth birthday - four nights at Disney World.

By night three, we'd found cameras at three different hotels.

Friday we checked into a five-star resort right near Magic Kingdom with three thousand positive reviews. Emma got her birthday button at the front desk and wore it all weekend.

Saturday we did the parks and came back exhausted around 9 PM. Emma showered and fell asleep so happy, and I remember thinking I'd given her the perfect birthday.

Sunday morning I went to brush my teeth and the bathroom was still humid from Emma's shower the night before.

I noticed the air freshener plugged into the outlet next to the mirror - the holes in the front grill looked off, not quite even.

I unplugged it and turned it over in my hands, and the back had tiny screws. I used my nail file to unscrew one and the casing popped open.

Camera - small circuit board, lens, SD card slot, battery pack.

I sat down hard on the bathroom floor and just stared at it, my hands shaking so badly I almost dropped it.

Emma had showered in here last night, right here, while this thing recorded her.

Someone had video of my thirteen-year-old daughter naked on her birthday.

I couldn't breathe, just sat there on the cold tile trying not to throw up.

Hotel security came within fifteen minutes and police came thirty minutes after that. They took the camera and the SD card, told us they'd investigate, and asked questions about when we checked in, what time Emma had showered, and who had access to our room.

We packed everything and left immediately. Emma was crying and asking why someone would ever do this, and I didn't have an answer - I just kept saying we were going somewhere safe.

Sunday night we checked into a completely different hotel - different brand, different area, four miles away from the first one.

I went into the bathroom first and checked everything, unplugged the air freshener, checked behind the mirror, looked at the smoke detector, felt under the sink - nothing.

The room felt clean.

Emma showered and I stood outside the door the entire time, then she went to bed around 10 PM and I sat in the chair next to her for an hour watching her sleep.

She said she felt safer here.

Monday morning around 7 AM she woke me up, standing next to my bed crying and holding the alarm clock from her nightstand. Her hands were shaking.

"Mom, look at this."

The back panel was loose - she'd woken up and noticed it wasn't flush against the rest of the clock, so she pulled it off to see why. Camera inside, lens pointing directly at her bed through a small hole in the speaker grill.

She'd slept there for eight hours and changed out of her pajamas in the morning. Changed into her swimsuit to go to the pool - someone had recorded all of it.

Emma sat on the edge of the bed and just shook, not crying anymore, just shaking and staring at the camera in her hands. I tried to take it from her but she wouldn't let go, just kept staring at it.

"They watched me sleep, they watched me get dressed - Mom, they watched me."

We left without checking out, didn't even talk to the front desk, just grabbed our bags and threw them in the car. Emma sat in the back seat the entire drive and didn't say a word, just stared out the window.

I found a third hotel with availability and checked in Monday afternoon, but this time I didn't wait.

Before I even brought Emma inside, I went to the car and dug through my trunk until I found the detector I'd bought months ago - one of those paranoid purchases you make and forget about.

I told Emma to wait in the lobby and I went to the room alone with the detector.

Started in the bathroom and scanned everything - clean. Bedroom next - scanned the smoke detector, the lamps, the picture frames, the outlets - clean.

Living area - scanned the TV, the DVD player, the decorative books on the shelf.

Picked up the TV remote from the coffee table and the detector went off.

I opened it with shaking hands and found a camera in the battery compartment, lens pointed at the couch where we'd be sitting. Where Emma would have been sitting in her pajamas watching TV before bed.

Three hotels, three cameras, three nights in a row.

I walked back to the lobby and Emma saw my face and just started crying - she knew. She didn't even ask, she just knew I'd found another one.

I called the police from the parking lot and told them I wasn't bringing my daughter into another room until someone explained what was happening.

They came and took the remote, and two hours later a detective showed up and asked to speak with me privately. He said they'd been investigating since Sunday and had checked all three hotels, finding cameras in eight other rooms - different families, all that week.

"We think it's the cleaning staff - they have master keys, they know checkout schedules, and we're finding the same camera models across six different Orlando hotels."

Six hotels, cleaning staff network, completely organized.

He asked me to send photos of Emma to identify her in recovered footage, so I sent three from that weekend - Emma in Mickey ears, Emma with Cinderella, Emma eating ice cream. Happy photos from before.

Wednesday afternoon he called and I was driving, had to pull over because my hands started shaking when I even heard his voice.

"We found your daughter in the footage - four different files, one from each hotel plus a duplicate from the first location. Bathroom and bedroom footage. Someone was collecting videos of her specifically."

Four videos - someone had gone through hundreds of files from dozens of families and pulled out every single one with Emma in it.

Made a collection of my thirteen-year-old daughter.

Horrifying.

"The buyer organized everything by child - age, appearance, location," the detective continued. "He was trading in a Telegram group with over four hundred members, and your daughter's files were downloaded two hundred and seventeen times."

Two hundred and seventeen people had videos of Emma getting ready for Disney, showering after the parks, sleeping, changing clothes, brushing her teeth - just being a thirteen year old girl.

We drove home Tuesday and never made it to Magic Kingdom for her actual birthday. Emma sat in the back seat for the entire eight-hour drive and barely spoke, and when we got home she went to her room and I heard her checking the smoke detectors, unplugging things, moving furniture to look behind it.

She still does that - every night before bed, checks every room in the house twice.

She won't travel anymore and I've tried to plan trips but she has panic attacks. She sleeps maybe four hours a night and showers with her phone on the counter playing music so she can't hear any sounds that might be cameras.

And I'm the mom who switched hotels thinking that would keep her safe, who didn't check immediately each time, who let her shower and sleep and change before I scanned the rooms.

The detective told me something I can't stop thinking about: "This isn't isolated to Orlando - same pattern in Vegas, LA, New York, Miami, cleaning staff networks, same buyers."

Every major tourist city - hotels, Airbnbs, vacation rentals, anywhere tourists go with their kids.

Cleaning staff have master keys and maintenance workers come to "fix things" while you're at dinner. They have access and they're organized.

The detective told me specifically that footage of kids at theme parks and teenagers on vacation is what the buyers want - collections organized by age.

You can't avoid it by reading reviews - the first hotel had five stars and thousands of positive reviews. Five-star resorts aren't safe.

There's only one way to know: check every room before your daughter uses it.

I check every hotel room now before Emma even sees it - bathrooms, bedrooms, living areas, takes ten minutes to scan completely. Ten minutes to know instead of finding out three days later that someone has a collection of your daughter.

Three hotels in four nights taught me you can't trust star ratings or brand names - you have to check.

I'm linking the detector I used below from this brand vigilant, the same one that found the third camera before Emma spent another night being recorded.

Hotels, Airbnbs, vacation rentals, any family destination - check before she showers, check before she sleeps, check before she changes.

Three different hotels in three nights taught me these cameras are EVERYWHERE and the only way to protect your daughter is to check, Every. Single. Time.

Emma deserved a magical thirteenth birthday but instead she can't sleep through the night anymore.

Please don't let that be your daughter.
Advice From A Cybersecurity Expert Who
